look_first: Turn the apparent flower sideways and underneath: find the receptacle and phyllary involucre, isolate a floret, then trace it to an inferior ovary and cypsela. Use the anther tube as a strong confirmation.

confusable.tie_breaker: Eryngium has individual 5-merous flowers and two-part dry fruit; Asteraceae has florets sharing a receptacle inside phyllaries, typically an anther tube, and one cypsela per floret.

exceptions: Baccharis and Ambrosia can lack showy rays.
A ray is a whole floret, not a petal.
Pappus may be bristles, scales, awns, a crown, or reduced or absent.
genus_routing: Route first by head type, then phyllaries, receptacle or paleae, pappus, cypsela, leaves and head array.
visuals: Ambrosia, Baccharis, Cirsium and Solidago exception strip
